title: run history files (<data-dir>/history)
description: Append-only, size-capped JSONL files of METADATA about the pipeline itself, so that restarts, stream holes and board reboots become data points instead of gaps in a log. One JSON object per line; every record has `k` (kind), `v` (record version, 1) and `t` (Unix seconds on the PC clock). Metadata only: no audio, no location. Each file rotates at its size cap to FILE.1 (one backup), so the total disk use is bounded (sink_history 32 MB, analyzer_history 48 MB, board_history 16 MB, run_ledger 16 MB, times two). Counters are cumulative since the producer's start: a reader takes deltas and treats a changed `started_t` / `started` as a counter reset. Readers MUST ignore unknown fields and unknown kinds.

sink_sample.description: sink_history.jsonl: one record per sink stats interval (30 s) from pc/bma_cable_sink.py: the sink_status.json fields that matter for stream health, cumulative since the sink process started at `started_t`.

started_t.description: Start time of the sink process; a change means the counters restarted from 0.

holes.description: Holes in the aligned 8-beam stream (a slot block missing past the reorder window).

playing.description: Instantaneous: the ring is past its prebuffer and playing.

analyzer_sample.description: analyzer_history.jsonl: one record per 30 s from analysis/host.py (status.json every 5 s, a compact sample of it every 30 s). `rx.gaps` is the SUM of the eight per-ring gap counters: divide by 8 for the number of loss events (the bridge counts each loss once). `plugins` maps an enabled plugin with counters to [windows, records, errors, dropped], cumulative since `started`; plugins without counters (novelty) and disabled ones are left out.

started.description: Analyzer process start; a change means the counters restarted from 0.

contiguous_s.description: Seconds of aligned audio all eight rings currently hold.

board_sample.description: board_history.jsonl: one record per @health record (about one a minute) that tools/bma_debug_rx.py already receives from the board; no board write, no extra socket. `boot_t` = host_t - up is derived and drifts by seconds per day (the board clock is free-running): never compare it exactly, use `boot_id` (fixed for the whole boot) to group samples.

t.description: PC time at receipt (the health record's host_t).

boot_t.description: t - up: the PC-clock time the board booted, as seen at this sample.

boot_id.description: int(boot_t) at the first sample of this boot; identical on every sample of the boot.

temp_remote_c.description: null when the board could not read the sensor.

seq.description: Datagram sequence of the health record.

board_boot.description: board_history.jsonl: written immediately before the first board_sample of a boot. A reboot is detected when the uptime falls by more than 1 s, or, on the first sample after the collector restarted, when boot_t differs from the last stored boot_t by more than 120 s. The very first record ever has null prev_* and gap_s.

prev_last_up.description: Last uptime seen before the reboot: the previous boot's lifetime lower bound.

gap_s.description: Seconds between the last sample of the previous boot and this one (the outage is somewhere inside it).

run_event.description: run_ledger.jsonl: appended by the supervisor (pc/run_pipeline.ps1 through pc/run_ledger.ps1). `ev` start | exit | supervisor_up | suppressed. `exit_code` is null with `exit_code_known` false when Windows reported none; 0 is a real exit code. A crash loop is bounded: at most 60 start/exit events per process per UTC hour are written, the rest are summarised by one `suppressed` record (with `count`) when the hour has passed. `version` is the first line of app\VERSION at the time of the event (null when the file is unreadable).

proc.description: analysis | classifier | bridge | board_debug | sink | ui | ambient | supervisor (open set).

uptime_s.description: On exit: seconds the process ran, when Windows knew its start and exit time.

count.description: Only on `suppressed`: events dropped for this process in that hour.
